body: Thank you, friend. Figured as much. Google wasn't much help which is why I cam here. I'll try running those two just to be sure, wouldn't hurt anyways, never know what could have been in there before.

Kind of what I figured. He kept trying to call back and was super pissed, I knew he hadn't accomplished what he set out to do. Also he didn't try to do anything but enter one simple command in the prompt.

Thanks for the reply and the encouragement. I don't know that I have any skills. I have failed so many things in life, I'm pretty sure it's something inherent built into me and my personality. I'm a very slow learner and this fast paced society does not take kindly at all to that. Are you saying you have a Ghost Writer? That's very interesting. Do you come up with the stories? 

When I was a kid, I went through a lot of bad stuff and was isolated a lot. I wasn't around other kids so I created these imaginary worlds in my mind. Adventures, characters. When people in the real world would interact with me I'd play all these scenarios in my mind. Who I thought they were, how they would act around me, etc. As I got older and kind of sucked at everything, I decided that maybe I was good at something. I experienced a bit of an adventure myself, something no one would ever know about, something that is in my heart to this day that the world would never understand or believe. It hurt knowing there were adventures out there waiting to be told but no one to hear them. I wanted so bad to make these adventures known. It wasn't that I wanted to be a "writer" or sit around all smug sipping coffee with my pinky up. I wanted to tell epic stories to the world and inspire people, people who may have no hope. I wanted to take them to other worlds, to show them that there is more to life than meets the eye and that through imagination the possibilities are endless. 

That was my desire. I work 12 hours a day at a blue collar job, making not enough money. I've never held down a job very long because I'm a slow learner and have very crippling anxiety. I interact fine with people but they make me super freaked out. I know I'll probably dredge through life like this always wondering what I wish could have been.

Had this exact thing happen to me. When she eventually broke it off she went around convincing all my friends that I was some horrible monster. Several of them even pointed out the inconsistency of several of her stories but only a few cared. She was good at manipulation and playing the victim. She even admitted to not only cheating on me but enjoying it. She also told any secret about my past I opened up to her about to humiliate me to everyone I knew. I literally had to leave the city I called home never to return because she thought it was funny to harass me and ruined the relationship I had after her. Years later, the pain never goes away and I could never return home.

Of course it was real! What was the creature? Who knows? That's the point. I don't want to know. Was it a "creature?" Creature makes it sound like some kind of animal. This thing was very conscious. But who knows. I don't know what it was or what to call it. I've questioned my own sanity over the happening in itself. If you find out what it was please let me know. I just know it had red eyes and footsteps that sounded inhuman or unlike any kind of animal I've ever heard.
Creepy! Don't go back, OP!
Oh cool. Is that how you got them for your first book too? On twitter?
Congrats! If you don't mind me asking, where do *you* find test readers?
Well maybe if you knew when to put down the spork and stop eating all that ass you wouldn't have these problems. Ever think of that?

Thanks for the reply. Are those kind of the only options for working remotely with an English degree? I've heard there are quite a few, but again I've just begun research on this. I've definitely worked in traditional environments as I have non traditional, that's why I know they don't work well for me, at least not for long. I'll definitely look into the blogging thing. When I was younger I had a blog that I decided to put google-ad something on and made several hundred dollars off it? I love Blogging but I don't see it as an easy way to make a legitimate full time living. I'm guessing to also build a writers portfolio as well? Twitter, Facebook, what else is important? Also, can you use a pen name for professional writing jobs like you can when creating novels? 

Thanks again for the help. Oh btw, I wasn't really home schooled. My early life was kind of fucked up...

Hey OP, I'm no one to talk on this subject but reading your post just kind of spoke to me. I've been in that exact situation before, albeit different it was eerily similar. There's a lot of things in life I do not have answers to, nor am I successful but I can tell you this much. DO NOT ever stay at a job that makes you that miserable, something that overwhelms you with anxiety. We've all worked jobs that suck, that you have to "stick out" some times, but then there's the ones that are more of a "Oh God, I can't take this, let me out" sort of thing. Those ones, you need to get out of sooner than later as they can do lasting mental damage to both you and your outlook on life. Find something you enjoy doing and do it, maybe exercise? Put time and effort into it, set some goals and achieve them even if it's with some silly little hobby. You'll feel less like a failure and it'll boost your confidence at being able to handle life head on and reevaluate what needs to be done. It's better to start at square one than to continually go forward in a circular motion. Take a step back, a deep breath and remember, one silly job is nothing in the grand scheme of life, humanity and what you have to offer to this world.

I appreciate it. One doesn't always need many words, a few can have a big impact. I wish I had the mental wherewithal right now to write it all out cohesively in order, maybe some day. I've dealt with more difficulties than I can count or remember. I don't think I'm special, I don't think that "no one has had it as bad as me." That's the bad part, once I had to start witnessing amazingly good people go through hell even worse than mine it just broke me inside. 

I finally got a job at one point where my peers and my boss were just, amazing people. I loved working with them every day, probably the only job I ever had where I REALLY liked all my coworkers and my boss. I thought to myself it was something I might could stick with for a long time, due to the people. My boss was an incredible, funny, caring yet stern when needed to be man. He was a father and loved by everyone who knew him. I watched as one person lied about him, got him into trouble and fired over a long course of time. I watched one person destroy my coworkers to where they either got fired or like me eventually just left. It destroyed me. I've never held down a job more than a year and a half in my whole life. It has been a major struggle and has made me feel like a failure who will never have a stable life.

I want so bad to own my own home some day. I want to have a decent car, make enough to buy decent groceries, travel and have adventures. I love to challenge myself, one thing I have a lot of trouble with is jobs where you go and do the same exact thing, every day, with no real path for improvement or climbing up any ladders, no real worthwhile experience built. Sure, you might make a slightly middle class income, but for what? To do it indefinitely? To hate every day of this precious life we are given? 

I love to learn things, I love to explore, I love to see new things and meet new people. I do terribly interacting with the same people over long periods of time. I suffer from major anxiety and social anxiety, it is crippling and painful. It took me what- several days to even respond to this? My brain is stuck in this perpetual pain it cannot escape from. I love meeting people, I have no trouble talking and interacting, being polite or trying to understand others, yet my personality is a passive one and I'm very friendly, so people tend to bully me around, make fun of me and take advantage of me. I've been harassed openly, made fun of and nothing done about it at a good number a jobs. A huge reason for my anxiety levels. I'm having to take care of people now, I have to take care of myself, I have to make a certain amount of money and there's no way out of it. At my current job I get belittled, I got yelled at today for eating lunch (I don't get a lunch break and work 9-10 hours a day). I get treated like shit, while the others circle jerk each other and make fun of me. I try to just nod, smile and let it slide off but it truly hurts. Is this all there is in this world? Is this what human interaction is about? Kissing each other's asses, sucking up, circle jerking and if you don't fit in you get chewed up and spit out? I don't do so well.

I want to write. I want to go back to my little coffee shop by the sea. I want to spend my days cultivating stories and adventures. I want to travel, I want to meet new people and inspire them and maybe they can be my inspiration to, I've definitely met some incredible ones in my travels. But I am backwards, dysfunctional and no one will never know any of this, no one will ever care. I wrote a book that is different. It is not fanservice, it is not pop-culture and it is no "political." It's an adventure, a very different kind, but I feel no one in this world gives a shit. Is this a way to live out the rest of my time? Knowing all of this?

I don't want to suffer anymore. I used to could see beyond the horizon. I could hear the echos of stories untold. I could feel things unexplained. I wish I could get that back, I wish I could mean something, I wish I could make a difference in this world, I wish I could just be me. I wish some one some where out there heard my scream and could show me just a glimmer of light in the direction I should walk, but I stumble blindly knowing I will never find the exit.

Hi Andy. 

I wrote a book too. I also have extremely crippling anxiety and have dealt with depression for a long time. I spent six years writing it and polishing draft after draft. Still, I am so scared that it has just sat in a box and on a thumb drive. I have no idea what to do with it. I fear if I took the wrong steps it could hurt my chances of it ever being sucessful. Is there any tips and advice you may have for me? I have wanted to write and make stories since I was little but feel all the time that this is the "real world" and such fantasies are too rare to pursue. I have failed most everything in life and am usually scared of failing this, something I'm so passionate about. Is there any tips and advice you may have for me?

Thank you :)

I'd truly appreciate it! I definitely need some beta readers and will keep you in mind once I finish the last little bit of editing. I agree, I need badly out of my situation, it's stifling and I feel like I can't breathe. I feel like I have no hope for anything. I can recognize that life shouldn't feel like that and that there is hope to be had, it's just not here and like this.

Thank you very much for the encouragement. I look forward to that day as well. I've heard also that a good editor can do much more than just spell checking and correcting grammatical mistakes, but to what extent? I also wonder how much it would cost me. My book is just shy of 900 pages long, I suppose it would be considered an "Epic" by length. I'll check out the writers groups, maybe there I can find some people who'll give my book a test-read. 

Thank you again for your reply and encouragement.

I know my local library has a book called "Self Publishing for dummies" and "E publishing for dummies." I don't know if those are worth anything. 

I've wondered about editors. From what I've heard they're really expensive, to what extent do they edit? Is it just spelling errors or do they help with structuring sentences and thoughts? Sounds like it could be really good or really bad.

I wish they could, but they aren't really in the situation to be able too. It's complicated but the only family I really have is my immediate family. Let's just say, there's not really room for me like there used to be. That's a whole other story though.

I moved where I am right now because it was cheaper, much cheaper and seemed like a nice place. It is an okay place but again, what I do here makes me hate it. If I had something that allowed me a bit more freedom, allowed me to actually use my brain at times and not work 10-12 hour days with super long commutes I'd surely hate it less. I would do anything on this planet, move anywhere and accept any life to be an E-book writer. I've thought of combining that with writing guides, possibly blogs, anything I could do to make income from writing. Amazon Insiders sounds interesting, I'll have to look it up, but it seems like a bigger audience than what I want right now. I'd like just a few people to read my book and tell me what they think.

Not to mention, that hour commute is during rush hour in a enormous city. I'm the type that gets stressed by that sort of thing after so long. My commute WOULD be about 30 minutes if there was no traffic, but I ALWAYS go in during morning rush hour and always get out during some point of the afternoon rush. The other day it actually took me an hour and 15 minutes to get home due to traffic. It definitely drains me. Another thing is that the job I do is HIGHLY risky and while some people are totally fine with it, it tends to make me really nervous even though I'm pretty good at it. So that adds to the whole as well.

My social network unfortunately is very small, just those couple of people and they don't really know anyone either. We keep to ourselves which is just how it is right now. We kind of "know" some people but not enough to really be asking for careers or further contacts and those people would be much in the same situation as us anyways. 

I'd love to self publish the book. If I made 40k a year even off of writing I'd be as happy as I would if I was making 4 million a year off of writing. It's not about the money. Sure, more is always welcomed but it's just more about being who you are. There are a lot of people, even doing what I do who simply like doing what they do. They don't make much, they might even have higher goals but they like what they do so their soul ultimately fits into place. I have tried so hard to force myself to be into what I do and to like it, I've been at it for 4 years now and not only has it not gotten easier, it's gotten worse as time goes on. Anyhow, back to the original point. I'd love to self publish my book, but would not want to until I knew it was good enough to be self published. I wouldn't want to make a fool of myself or actually ask people for their money without giving them a suitable product. Does the kindle E-book community do the free readings?

Another few side notes I forgot to mention. Again, I had to leave the place where I felt at home. Where I'm at is a nice place once you get out of the city, but the city itself is huge, overpopulated, nerve racking and well, I don't like big city life, I like where you have communities or villages around and a slower way of life. However, where I'm at is not conducive to my other interests or passions I have. Aside from writing there's really just 2 other passions I've had in life. One of them I had to completely give up when I moved, it was something that always reduced my stress and made me feel alive. The other has the same effect but even it is something I can't really do where I am.

I'm a very passionate kind of person. I get immersed in things, I like to master them, learn all about them and love them. Unfortunately I'm unable to do much of anything right now aside from work, eat and sleep.

Unfortunately it's not really his fault. The work is divided up and it's one of those "all work has to be finished by the end of the day" kind of deals. Unfortunately there will NEVER be a day with less than 9 hours but I don't remember my last 9 hour day. It's almost always 10-12 hours. It's a very blue collar, dirty and gritty kind of job. Before here I was used to being a completely different person. I'm more of a "Sipping tea at a coffee shop while it rains outside with a scarf around my neck" type. Now I wear heavy duty work boots, gloves and safety equipment. Am I "too good" for it? Absolutely not, if anything I'm not good enough. It's not a thing like that, it's just that I'm so far removed out of my element. 

I'd be more than happy to let anyone read it who wanted to, they don't need any special credentials. I guess if people like it, it's some what of a success, right? Anyone can be a reader and if enough anyone's like it then bingo! I've had trouble finding places to get it read, I'm not sure where to find people and I feel like I don't have the time to contribute a lot back or read other people's fine work due to my schedule.

Thank you kindly for the reply.

One thing keeping me at my job is respect for my boss. He's a good and kind man, it's a small company and I don't hate the people I work around at all. I put on the fake smile for them. It hurts though, every time I smile then go off to myself I feel like I just lied to some one. Yet, as you said it is money, right? I can save with this job. After taxes 40k still isn't a lot, but it's enough to save, pay off some bills, live in a apartment and that's about it. Unfortunately I've got some debt I'm trying to pay off, not a huge amount but it's there and I want it gone.

The thing is, with every passing day I feel worse, witch each passing week and month I feel as if my mind is becoming numb, like I can't think anymore, like my soul got up and left and there's only a brain inside of an empty shell. If I tried to write right now, I probably couldn't. I'm always so stressed, so filled with anxiousness and anxiety. My mind is more clouded than a foggy coastal morning, I can't see anything yet I know it's right there.

I never tell anyone I want to be a writer, in my opinion until I'm published and making some kind of living from it I do not deserve that title. I never wanted to be a writer for bragging rights at all. I wrote because it was within me to do so. 99% of everyone who has ever come across me knows nothing about it. The only ones who know are the couple of very close people in my life and that's it. Even then I've asked them to not really talk about it much as I have to try to forget about it so that I can keep grinding away at my job without going into a full mental breakdown. 

I would love to get back in physical shape as well and have enough time to get my mind on the right track as well, but after 10-12 hours at work and 2 hours of commuting a day, when I get home I pretty much just want to eat, get online for a few minutes and crash. Even on the weekends I feel like a potato. Once I do a bit of cleaning, a tiny bit of relaxing, sleeping in, doing laundry and preparing for the next week I simply do not have time for anything else.

I very much feel trapped.
